Dispatch channels

Dispatch channels open incidents: the model pulls the address, units and call type from each dispatch. Tactical channels (fireground, EMS ops) only update an incident that already involves one of the units heard. A fixed call type overrides the model for a channel that carries one kind of traffic.

Places

Hospitals, stations and landmarks, with the channels that belong to them. A place on the map lets a tripwire say how far away something is, and which hospital nearest the call can take it.

No places yet. If your catalog names the hospital channels, “Add from my catalog” fills this in.
Home & geocoding

Addresses are looked up on OpenStreetMap's Nominatim, at most one per second with a cache, as their usage policy asks. Point this at your own Nominatim or Photon-compatible server for volume.

Follow-ups for

Follow-ups go out as Telegram replies to the first message, so an incident reads as one thread — at most 10 replies. What that radio says next follows the unit that tripped it onto any talkgroup (a medic calling the hospital); everything on the talkgroup is for quiet channels.

Appearance

            

              
Theme

              

              
Colour schemes, including the seasons and the Speedway; Amber and Terminal switch to a monospace type throughout for a phosphor-CRT look. Changes apply instantly.

              
Fonts override the scheme's type

              
Body

              
Monospace (IDs, times, transcripts' small print)

              
Headings

              
Text size scales the whole interface

              

              
Top tabs drag a tab to reorder them

              
Monitor, Library, Conversations, Dispatch, Settings. Everything else lives in this left-hand menu.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Scanning

            

              

                
                
              

              

                
                
              

              
              
              
              
Gain and frequency correction live in the Devices tab; radio and sample rate are in the top bar. Airspy at 10 M covers a whole site (±3.84 MHz); 2.5 M covers ±0.96 MHz; RTL-SDR covers ±1.2 MHz. The follower measures and compensates tuner error on its own; ppm keeps the radio centred where the band centre says, which matters at the band edges.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Transcription

            

              
              

                
                
                
              

              

                
                
              

              
Models on this machine download once, then transcription starts instantly · delete the ones you no longer use 

              
Modelfaster-whisperopenai-whispermlx-whisper

              
Runs locally with Python. On an Apple-silicon Mac use pip install mlx-whisper: it runs on the GPU and leaves the CPU to the radio (a CPU-bound transcription starves the decoder and chops the audio). Elsewhere pip install faster-whisper (CPU, capped at a few cores here) or openai-whisper (CPU, all cores). Models download on first use.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Transcript corrections

            

              
Misheard → correct phrase replacements, "Rirey" → "Riley". Leave the TG field blank to apply a rule to every talkgroup, or set one to scope it.

Audio & recording

            

              

                
                
                
              

              
WAV is always captured first; other formats are made by ffmpeg and replace it. Speech at 8 kHz sounds fine at 24–32 kbit/s.

              

                
                
              

              
              
              

              

                
                
                
              

              
Per-talkgroup exceptions are set in the Aliases tab (Rec · Str · Up). A call that is not recorded still appears in the call history and library, without audio.

              

                
                
              

              

                

                  
                  
                

              

              
            

          

        

        

          

            
Remote access · phone over Tailscale

            

              
              
              
From a phone on your tailnet, open the address and enter the token — the same live feed, calls, and audio as the desktop.

              
              
Lets your other devices (and other copies of HoosierSDR) open this one without typing the token — verified with tailscale whois, only for Tailscale addresses. Turn it on at both ends, or paste the other instance's token below.

            

          

          

            
Instances on your tailnet · other copies of HoosierSDR

            

              

                Checking Tailscale…
                
              

              

              
Every online device on the account is checked for a running HoosierSDR. Open shows that instance live in its own window — its feed, calls, and audio as they happen. It needs a token from that machine's Remote access page unless it trusts this account.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Share calls · rdio-scanner / OpenMHz / Broadcastify Calls

            

              
              

                
                
                
              

              
              

                
                
                
              

              
              

                
                
                
              

              

                
                
              

              
Each call is sent once per service after it completes (WAV to rdio-scanner; M4A/MP3 via ffmpeg to OpenMHz and Broadcastify). Outcomes are kept per call; re-send from a call's detail in the Library.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Script hook · run a program after each call

            

              
              
              

                
                
                
              

              

              

              
The call arrives as environment variables — HS_TG, HS_TG_NAME, HS_UNIT, HS_UNIT_NAME, HS_FREQ_HZ, HS_SECS, HS_EMERGENCY, HS_AUDIO, HS_JSON, HS_SYSTEM, HS_TALKER_ALIAS — and as one JSON object on standard input. Runs off the decode thread, one at a time.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Live feed · Icecast / Broadcastify

            

              
              

                
                
                
              

              

                
                
                
              

              

                
                
                
              

              

                
                
              

              
Broadcastify feeds: use the host, port, mount and source password from your feed's "Feed Technical Details" page. Encoding and connection are done by ffmpeg.

Alias sources

            

              

              
Each RadioReference system you load (Playlists → Load) and each CSV you import is kept here and merged; the newest source wins when two name the same talkgroup. Priority, alert, avoid and lock-out are your own settings and apply whichever source names the talkgroup — the same model as SDRTrunk's alias lists.

            

          

          

            
Talkgroup ranges

            

              

                
                
                
              

              

                
                
                
              

              

              
A rule covers every talkgroup in the range — the way SDRTrunk alias ranges and OP25 whitelists work. Explicit per-talkgroup settings win over a range; the engine applies lock-out and priority ranges natively.

Chats the bot can see

            

              

              
None found yet. Message the bot (or send /start@yourbot in a group topic), then press Find chats. Telegram keeps a bot's messages for a day, so do it shortly before.

A person's chat id looks like 123456789, a group's like -1001234567890. A topic id is the last number in a topic's link (t.me/c/…/57).

AI · cloud model

            

              

                
                
              

              

                
                
              

              
              

              
For rules and the dispatch map set to "Cloud". OpenRouter reaches Claude and GPT through one key (model e.g. anthropic/claude-opus-4.1 or openai/gpt-4o). Choose Anthropic or OpenAI to go direct (models claude-opus-4-8, gpt-4o). The key never leaves this machine; extraction runs in the app.

            

          

        

      

        

        

      

        

          

            
Attached radios

            

              

              
No radio detected. Plug in an Airspy or RTL-SDR and press Rescan.

              
The top-bar Radio picker lists these. On start-up the app picks the saved radio if it is attached, otherwise the first Airspy, otherwise the first RTL-SDR.

            

          

        

        

          

            
Band coverage · the other radios

            

              
The radio picked in the top bar holds the control channel. Every other attached radio marked cover is parked on a part of the site's span the primary cannot see, so calls granted there are decoded too — the way Unitrunker spreads a site over several tuners.
